blocks.html:
Module 5 of 5. Show up credibly, move qualified prospects through the B.U.Y.E.R.S. Journey, and bring in a managing principal to close.

Here's how this module works: watch the video, work through a few short sections, answer a quick knowledge check, respond to a scenario (your coach grades it, and 3 of 4 points passes), then build one piece of your personal Sales Game Plan.

blocks.title: OneAccord Sales Video 5 - How to Close Deals. Establish Trust and Build Credibility

links.label: Video won't play? Open it in SharePoint

blocks.html:
1. Show up as a giver

  • A solo consultant treats every meeting like a job interview and shows up transactional. At OneAccord you show up as a giver, not a taker, backed by a 25-year firm that has served 650+ businesses.
  • It's a consultative sale from the start: sit on the same side of the table as the owner. Don't be a hammer that sees every problem as a nail.
  • Be humble, hungry and smart, with no false humility. Be truthful about our track record and our people's experience.
  • Values are a lifestyle, not a switch: truth, compassion and service, including delivering hard news in a way the client can hear.

2. How you show up

Do
ZoomUse the OneAccord background or a clean, professional space. No calls from the kitchen.
AttireMatch the client's environment: no suit and tie at an agriculture client, and no jeans and a T-shirt at a professional services firm.
MannerismsListen more than you talk. Be on time. Follow up when you said you would.
Collateral and slidesOnly current, OneAccord-branded materials.
ProofTestimonials, case studies and client videos, available through the OneAccord Sales Coach.

3. You don't close alone

Your job is to bring the engagement "into orbit." Then a managing principal helps take it over the finish line.

  • Only managing principals can issue a statement of work and scope or price work. Everyone in the sales process works with one at some point.
  • Bring yours in once a prospect is qualified and moving from Understand toward Yearning.
  • Position it to the client as serving them: "I'd like to bring one of our managing principals to our next meeting. They know your industry and will serve you best."
  • Internally, it's alignment, not a handoff. You stay involved.

4. The B.U.Y.E.R.S. Journey

Services are bought, not sold. Help prospects through six stages. Move a prospect to the next stage only when they show it, ideally in their own words.

StageThe prospect…
BotheredCan identify the problem and expresses a sense of urgency
UnderstandCan articulate the scope of the problem and the desired outcome and asks how to achieve it
YearningExplicitly states desire ("This is what I need") and can describe the approach in their own words
ExplainableCan explain the value in their own words and defend the decision to stakeholders
ReadyGives a specific verbal commitment ("I'm in!") and confirms final approval
StartedSigns the contract and submits payment and commits resources

In Zoho you'll also see Finished: the engagement has been delivered.

5. The eight rules

  1. Don't skip steps.
  2. No urgency = no opportunity.
  3. To yearn, they must understand.
  4. Yearning must be verbal and mutual.
  5. Buyers must be able to justify their decision.
  6. Enthusiasm ≠ commitment.
  7. If it isn't paid for, it isn't a deal yet.
  8. Celebrate the chance to deliver value.

In Zoho CRM: keep each opportunity's B.U.Y.E.R.S. stage current, and record the buyer's own words as evidence. For the how-to, see Lesson 5: Working the Buyer's Journey in the Zoho CRM Training Coach.

blocks.prompt: Who can issue a statement of work and price an engagement?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Bring your managing principal in at the right time.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Only managing principals scope and price work.

blocks.prompt: A prospect says, "This is exactly what we need," and describes your approach back to you in his own words. Which stage is he in?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. He stated the desire and described the approach himself: Yearning.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: That's Yearning: an explicit desire plus the approach in his own words.

blocks.prompt: An owner is excited and says, "Let's do it!" but hasn't confirmed approval with his partners. Which rule applies?
options: Celebrate the chance to deliver value
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. He isn't Ready until final approval is confirmed.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Enthusiasm ≠ commitment. Ready requires final approval.

blocks.prompt: What must be true for a prospect to be Bothered?
options: They can identify the problem and express urgency
They were referred by a partner
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Bothered means they can name the problem and feel urgency.

blocks.prompt: A verbal "I'm in" and final approval are confirmed, but no contract has been signed. Which stage are they in?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. They're Started only once the contract is signed, paid for, and resourced.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: They're Ready. Started requires a signed contract, payment and committed resources.

blocks.prompt: You're meeting a farm-equipment manufacturer on site. What should you wear?
options: Business casual that fits their environment
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Match their environment. Business casual fits here.

blocks.promptHtml:
A prospect has named the problem, feels real urgency, and has described the outcome he wants. He just asked: "So how would you actually fix this?" You're three months in as a principal.

Where is he on the B.U.Y.E.R.S. Journey, what's your next move, and when does your managing principal come in?
rubric: Correctly places him at Understand, moving toward Yearning
Proposes a next step that helps him articulate the approach himself, rather than pushing to close
Brings in a managing principal at the right point and positions it as serving the client
Mentions logging the stage and his own words as evidence in Zoho

Humble, hungry and smart, no false humility. Values (truth, compassion, service) are a lifestyle. AND confirms final approval), Started (signs contract AND pays AND commits resources). Zoho adds Finished (delivered). 8 rules: don't skip steps; no urgency = no opportunity; to yearn they must understand; yearning must be verbal and mutual; buyers must be able to justify their decision; enthusiasm is not commitment; if it isn't paid for it isn't a deal; celebrate the chance to deliver value. Keep the stage current in Zoho and record the buyer's own words as evidence.

blocks.title: My Pipeline on B.U.Y.E.R.S.
blocks.promptHtml: Take 2–3 live opportunities and place each one honestly on the B.U.Y.E.R.S. Journey. Then write your personal show-up checklist.

fields.label: For each opportunity: current stage, the buyer's own words that prove it, your next action, and whether a managing principal is involved
My 5-item show-up checklist (Zoom, attire, materials, habits)

criteria: Each stage is backed by buyer evidence (their words or actions), not optimism
Next actions are buyer-led and advance one stage at a time
A managing principal is involved where scoping or pricing is near
The show-up checklist is specific and practical
